etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English whether, whather, from Old English hweþer, hwæþer, from Proto-West Germanic *hwaþar, from Proto-Germanic *hwaþeraz, comparative form of *hwaz (“who”). Cognate with German weder (“neither”), Swedish var, Icelandic hvor (“each of two, which of two”).

definitions.definition: Indicates doubt between possibilities (usually with correlative or).

quote.citation: 1915, G[eorge] A. Birmingham [pseudonym; James Owen Hannay], chapter I, in Gossamer, New York, N.Y.: George H. Doran Company, →OCLC:
quote.text: As a political system democracy seems to me extraordinarily foolish, […]. My servant is, so far as I am concerned, welcome to as many votes as he can get. […] I do not suppose that it matters much in reality whether laws are made by dukes or cornerboys, but I like, as far as possible, to associate with gentlemen in private life.

quote.citation: 2012 June 19, Phil McNulty, “England 1–0 Ukraine”, in BBC Sport:
quote.text: The incident immediately revived the debate about goal-line technology, with a final decision on whether it is introduced expected to be taken in Zurich on 5 July.

quote.citation: 2013 July 20, “Old soldiers?”, in The Economist, volume 408, number 8845:
quote.text: Whether modern, industrial man is less or more warlike than his hunter-gatherer ancestors is impossible to determine. The machine gun is so much more lethal than the bow and arrow that comparisons are meaningless. One thing that is true, though, is that murder rates have fallen over the centuries, as policing has spread and the routine carrying of weapons has diminished.

definitions.definition: Without a correlative, introduces a simple indirect question.
Introduces a disjunctive adverbial clause qualifying the main clause (with correlative or).

quote.citation: 1931 April, Francis Younghusband, “Preface”, in The Epic of Mount Everest‎[1], London: Edward Arnold & Co., →OCLC, →OL, page 5:
quote.text: The years have gone by and still we know not whether or no Mallory and Irvine reached the summit. But the will to climb Mount Everest is still alive.

definitions.definition: (obsolete) Introduces a direct question between alternatives (often with correlative or).

quote.text: whether ys it easyer to saye to the sicke of the palsey, thy synnes ar forgeven the: or to saye, aryse, take uppe thy beed and walke?

quote.citation: 1726 October 28, [Jonathan Swift], Travels into Several Remote Nations of the World.  […]  [Gulliver’s Travels], volume I, London:  […]  Benj[amin] Motte, […], →OCLC, part II (A Voyage to Brobdingnag):
quote.text: On the 17th, we came in full view of a great island, or continent (for we knew not whether;) on the south side whereof was a small neck of land jutting out into the sea, and a creek too shallow to hold a ship of above one hundred tons.
"Whether is better, the gift or the donor? / Come to me," / Quoth the pine tree, "I am the giver of honor."
